stem: An online store keeps its orders in an Amazon DynamoDB table in provisioned capacity mode, and a mission-critical checkout API reads and writes items in the table. Two other workloads use most of the read capacity. A status page calls GetItem with strongly consistent reads for single orders, and the page can show data that is a few seconds old. Each night, a report job runs a Scan of the whole table with a filter expression that returns the orders whose status is OPEN; few orders are open at any time. The reads of the checkout API are throttled. Which TWO actions will reduce the read capacity that the two workloads consume in the MOST cost-effective way? (Select TWO.)
keywords: can show data that is a few seconds old
returns the orders whose status is OPEN
few orders are open at any time

options.text: Make the filter expression of the nightly Scan more selective, so that the Scan returns fewer order items to the report job.
options.why: A filter runs after the read, so the Scan still [consumes the same amount of read capacity](../facts/dynamodb.md#dynamodb-scan-filter-same-read-capacity) as without it.

options.text: Add an attribute that only open orders carry, create a global secondary index on that attribute, and change the report job to query that index.
options.why: The index [only tracks data items](../facts/dynamodb.md#dynamodb-gsi-only-items-with-key-attributes) that carry its key, so it is [faster and less expensive to query that index](../facts/dynamodb.md#dynamodb-sparse-index-faster-cheaper-than-scan).

options.text: Create a DAX cluster, and send the strongly consistent GetItem calls of the status page through the DAX client so that DAX serves them from memory.
options.why: [DAX passes strongly consistent read requests to DynamoDB](../facts/dax.md#dax-passes-through-strong-reads-and-transactions) without a cache, so the table still serves every one of these reads.

options.text: Change the GetItem calls of the status page from strongly consistent reads to eventually consistent reads by setting ConsistentRead to false.
options.why: [Eventually consistent reads](../facts/dynamodb.md#dynamodb-eventually-consistent-half-cost) cost [half the cost of strongly consistent reads](../facts/dynamodb.md#dynamodb-eventually-consistent-half-cost), and the page accepts older data.

options.text: Copy each open order into a second table with a Lambda function on the stream of the table, and change the report job to scan the second table.
options.why: It also lowers the reads of the table, but the company then pays for a second table, a Lambda function and a write for every copied order.
options.misconception: A copy that custom code keeps in sync is the cheapest way to take a report off a table.

explanation: Each workload needs its own fix. The report filters after it reads, so it [consumes the same amount of read capacity](../facts/dynamodb.md#dynamodb-scan-filter-same-read-capacity) as an unfiltered Scan; a sparse index [only tracks data items](../facts/dynamodb.md#dynamodb-gsi-only-items-with-key-attributes) that carry its key attribute. The status page accepts older data, and [Eventually consistent reads](../facts/dynamodb.md#dynamodb-eventually-consistent-half-cost) cost half as much.
takeaway: Filters and DAX do not cut these reads; a sparse index and eventually consistent reads do.
twin: If the stem said "the status page must show the latest write" instead: keep its strongly consistent reads, because they return the [most up-to-date data](../facts/dynamodb.md#dynamodb-consistentread-parameter).
say: For the report I query a sparse index, and for the status page I use eventually consistent reads.
